title: Defining functions
learningGoals: call a function by its name and brackets
call one function from inside another

youtube.title: Python Functions: def and Calling | Python Programming EP 41
youtube.description: In this episode you will define a function with def, call a function by its name and brackets and call one function from inside another, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Your own tools · 0:56 Define and call · 1:36 What a call does · 2:08 Second program · 3:08 Recap · 3:39 Bug of the Day · 4:27 Challenge · 4:47 Next episode

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Until now every program was one long script. Today we learn to name a block of code, and reuse it.

scenes.onScreen: "Your own tools": three numbered lines (1. def names a block of code; 2. The body is indented under the def line; 3. A call runs the body, as often as you like) and an analogy card: a recipe card: you write the steps once, then cook the dish whenever you like by naming the card
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A function is a named block of code. You write it once with def, a name, brackets and a colon. The body is indented below. Nothing runs until you call it, by writing its name with brackets. Think of a recipe card. You write the steps once, then cook the dish whenever you like by naming the card. Functions stop you repeating yourself, and they give your code names that explain what it does.

scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right; faint indent guide lines
scenes.narration: [HL 1] The word def, a name, empty brackets, and a colon. This line only makes the function. It does not run it. [HL 2] The body is indented. This is what runs on every call. [HL 3] A call. The name, with brackets. Python jumps up to the body, runs it, and comes back. [HL 4] A second call. The same body runs again. Write once, use many times.

code.source:
def greet():
    print("Hello from a function")
greet()
greet()
code.output:

Hello from a function

scenes.onScreen: Call flow: the call line, the def, the body, and the return to the next line
scenes.animation: A call arrow jumps from the call line up to the def, the body lines light up one by one, then the arrow returns to the line after the call
scenes.narration: Here is the journey of a call. Python reaches the call line. It jumps up to the def, and runs the body, line by line. When the body ends, Python returns to the line just after the call, and carries on. Defining a function does nothing by itself. Only a call sends Python on this trip.

scenes.onScreen: banner.py: a banner built from two small functions
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 1] A small function that prints ten dashes. [HL 2] Its body. [HL 3] A second function, called title. [HL 4] Inside it, we call line. [HL 5] Print the word. [HL 6] And call line again. [HL 7] One call to title runs the whole banner. Small functions that do one job, combined, make big programs easy to read.

code.source:
def line():
    print("-" * 10)
def title():
    line()
    print("KONKANI")
    line()
title()

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the command types with key-tick, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as banner dot py. In the terminal, type python, space, banner dot py. A line of dashes, the word KONKANI, and another line of dashes.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One: def makes a function, and the body is indented below it. Two: Nothing runs until the function is called with brackets. Three: A function can call other functions. Four: Write it once, call it as often as you like. Pause the video, and say these ideas out loud, once, slowly.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: defined but never called
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We define the function hello, and run the program. Nothing happens. No error, and no output. A def only makes the function. It does not run it. Add a call, the name with brackets, and Hi appears. If a function seems to do nothing, check that you actually call it.

scenes.onScreen: Why did the function never get tired? It was always called back.

shorts.title: What is a function?
shorts.hook: "A function is a named block of code."
shorts.script: A function is a named block of code. You write it once with def, a name, brackets, and a colon. The body is indented below. Then you can use it as many times as you like by calling its name. Think of a recipe card. Write the steps once, and cook the dish whenever you want. Functions stop you repeating yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Write once, use often.

shorts.title: Define versus call
shorts.hook: "Here is the most important idea about functions."
shorts.script: Here is the most important idea about functions. Defining and calling are two different things. The def line only makes the function. Nothing runs. A call, the name with brackets, runs the body. When Python reaches a call, it jumps up to the body, runs it, and comes back to the next line. Two steps, always. Pause the video and type it out yourself. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Two separate steps.

shorts.title: Functions calling functions
shorts.script: A function can call another function. A title function can call a line function, print a word, and call the line function again. One call to title runs all of it. Small functions that do one job each are easy to read, easy to test, and easy to reuse. Build big things from small, named pieces. Say it out loud once. Then you remember it. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Small pieces, big programs.

shorts.title: The function that did nothing
shorts.script: A quiet bug. You write a function, run the program, and nothing happens. No error, no output. You only defined the function, and never called it. A def makes the function, it does not run it. Add the call, the name with brackets, and your function finally does its job. Check for the call first. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Did you call it?

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the function never get tired?"
shorts.script: Why did the function never get tired? It was always called back. Your challenge. Write a function called welcome. Inside, print two lines of greeting. Then call the function three times, one after another. You should see six lines on the screen. Try changing the text inside the function, and see all three calls change together. Share it below. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 41.
shorts.caption: Try your first function.
